text.text: Copy this outline into a new spec. Keep each section short; a good spec fits on two screens.
Two sentences: what we will build and why now.
What problem are we solving, for whom?
How will we know it worked?
What are we deliberately not doing?
The approach, with a diagram if it helps. Name the components and who owns them.
What it is, and why we did not choose it.
What it is, and why we did not choose it.
What could go wrong, and how will we notice?
Enable for ten percent of customers.
Security review, if it touches data or sign-in

text.text: Write a short spec before building anything that is hard to undo. Reviewers comment, the author decides, and the decision is logged.
Open any spec to find the full outline (problem, goals, design, risks, rollout) already inside it.
the spec from the outline and set a review deadline at least five working days out.
one named reviewer and post the link in the engineering channel.
in the doc. Reviewers say what they would change and why.
by the deadline. The author makes the call and writes the reason.
the decision, mark the spec Approved, and link follow-up tasks.
When a spec is not needed
Reversible changes under a few days of work do not need a spec.
When to ask for a second reviewer
Security, billing or anything touching customer data.
A decision is one sentence and the reason behind it. Log it the day it is made, link it to the spec it belongs to, and nobody has to remember why in a year.
Write the reason, not just the choice. “We chose Postgres” ages badly; “We chose Postgres because reporting needs joins” does not.
